hints.title: Solve each inequality first
hints.body: Factor the quadratic and solve its inequality. Solve the linear inequality separately.
hints.recap: Both conditions must hold for the same x.
hints.pitfall: Multiplying the two original expressions does not automatically represent “both”.
hints.pause: Draw the two solution sets on the same number line.

recall.reminder: Both conditions must hold for the same x.

hints.title: Use the ends of the overlap
hints.body: Keep only the overlap. Make a quadratic with roots at its two ends by multiplying two linear factors.
hints.recap: A quadratic with positive leading coefficient is negative between its two distinct roots.
hints.pitfall: The original inequalities are strict, so do not include their boundary points.
hints.pause: Expand your factors and choose the inequality giving precisely that overlap.

recall.reminder: A quadratic with positive leading coefficient is negative between its two distinct roots.

solution:
The first inequality is (x−2)(x−6)<0, giving 2<x<6. The second is 2x>8, or x>4. Thus their common solution set is 4<x<6.

The quadratic (x−4)(x−6) has a positive leading coefficient, so it is negative exactly between those roots. Expanding yields x2−10x+24<0, option C. This gives the whole intersection, with both endpoints excluded.
knowledgePattern: Intersect two inequality intervals then encode the result as a quadratic
